evidence: Cic. Top. 8: argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: an argument resting chiefly on facts, where ratiō rests on reasoning. Also the plot of a play or a story (see subject).

evidence: Cic. N.D. 3.9: sī quid est ēvidēns, dē quō inter omnīs conveniat, argūmentārī
terms.comment: To argue that something is so, with an accusative and infinitive: contendere (see claim).

phrases.latin: itaque licet dēfīnīre locum esse argūmentī sēdem, argūmentum autem ratiōnem, quae reī dubiae faciat fidem
phrases.english: so we may define a topic as the home of an argument, and an argument as reasoning that makes a doubtful point believable

sources: Lewis & Short: argumentum · Lewis & Short: argumentor
